palette.notes: Biome colour families: saturated grass green and sky blue on the surface, brown dirt, orange-red lava in the underworld, dark purple-brown caves. Shadows go to blue-grey and near black; items are bright and saturated so they pop on dark ground. No metrics file.

lighting: Tile lighting: surface scenes are evenly lit, underground falls to near black with soft light around torches and the player; lava glows and lights the cave red. Day/night shifts smoothly (wiki).
silhouette: Player and NPCs are small (about 3 tiles tall), chunky, with clear heads and gear (a blue wizard hat and robe reads at once); items get a dark outline and a single bright colour, so even a 16 px icon reads.

motion.timing: Short walk and swing cycles; weapon swings arc around the player and leave trails, hits pop floating damage numbers. No frame timings measured.

texture: Tile terrain with ore specks, grass tufts and brick patterns; visible chunky pixels when zoomed. Late-game bosses are big, detailed sprites with glowing eyes and particle sparks.
camera: Side-on view following the player; scale contrast does the drama: a tiny player under a boss that fills the screen. Fan clips zoom hard into single sprites.

acting.enters: A Guide greets the player at the start; other NPCs move into built houses once goals are met (wiki).
acting.acts: NPCs stand in a row with the player and a slime, each in their own outfit; they wander homes, react to biome and neighbours, and sell items (wiki).
acting.exits: NPCs can die or leave, then move back in when a house is free (wiki).
acting.depth: One plane of play with a parallax treeline and hills behind it; a giant boss fills the background while the player is a dot in front.

techniques: biome colour families for instant place reading
darkness everywhere except around light sources
dark outline + one bright colour per item icon
tiny hero against a screen-filling boss for scale drama
floating damage numbers as hit feedback
feel: biome colour + dark caves with lit pockets + chunky readable sprites + floating numbers = cozy, legible sandbox
for_fred: Give every prop Fred touches a dark outline and one bright colour so it reads at phone size. For a big moment, flip the scale: show something huge behind Fred while he is a small dot in front, and pop a floating number or word when he lands a hit. Let Pixie idle small in the background like an NPC.
